title: MUIDS Interview — B1 (Ploy)
setting: Classroom practice dialog in an interview room. Two characters: an interviewer and a 14-year-old student.

characters.name: Teacher
characters.voice_notes: Authoritative adult male interviewer, professional, clear conversational delivery

characters.name: Ploy
characters.voice_notes: Teenage girl, slightly nervous at first, natural conversational
characters.key_line: "Good morning. Well, my name is Ploy, and I'm fourteen."

turns.line: Good morning. Please, have a seat. So, tell me about yourself.
Good morning. Well, my name is Ploy, and I'm fourteen. I go to school in Bangkok. When I'm not studying, I play volleyball, and I like reading adventure books. In the future, I want to be a doctor.
Nice. So why do you want to study at em-yoo-eye-dee-es?

Because of the way they teach. Students learn by doing things, not just reading. For example, science students do real experiments and present them in English. I want to study medicine, so I need strong English and practical skills. So em-yoo-eye-dee-es is exactly the school I want.
Science, for sure! I love knowing how things work. For example, last term we did an experiment with magnets. So yeah, that's why science is my favourite.
Another question. Should phones be banned at school?
Hmm, no. I don't think phones should be banned. They're really useful for learning. For example, I can look up a word on my phone in seconds. So I think they should stay, just not during tests.
Good answer. What do you do when you face a challenge?
Last year, I had a really hard maths exam. I was nervous, so I made a study plan and practiced every day. In the end, I passed, and I felt so proud.
Very good. Do you have any questions for us?
Yes. What's a normal day at em-yoo-eye-dee-es like?
We start at eight thirty, and we have five classes a day. Thank you for coming. We'll let you know our decision soon.
